  description: 'MECHANISM PROFILE — context-mismatched spinlock (missing bottom-half disable). UNTRUSTED SOURCE: not attacker-supplied data but attacker-influenced concurrency triggers — any packet/event that executes the device''s softirq-context callback (ndo_start_xmit under NET_TX softirq, timer-driven xmit) while a process-context path (workqueue worker, ioctl, open/firmware/SME request) holds the same lock on that CPU; local or remote traffic and timer expiry are enough to align both sides. MISSING GUARANTEE: lock-context discipline — a spinlock reachable from softirq/timer context must be acquired with spin_lock_bh()/local_bh_disable() at every process-context site; plain spin_lock() only disables preemption, not bottom halves, so a softirq can run on the same CPU between lock and unlock. UNSAFE USE: process call chain (worker -> driver helper -> hw_tx/enqueue) holds the plain-acquired lock, then a softirq on the same CPU spins forever trying to take that same lock while the holder can never resume — a self-deadlock. CONSEQUENCE: softirq/soft-lockup on one CPU, RCU stall and watchdog splats, device TX stall, repeatable denial of service. The invariant generalizes one level up: a lock shared with a hardirq handler needs irqsave/irq-disable at non-irq sites. Seed (staging ks7010 tx_dev_lock, workqueue xmit path vs xmit callback) is a demonstration only and must never be reported. BRANCHES: branch1=xmit-softirq-lock: in net/wireless/staging drivers, find lock objects taken with plain spin_lock in process/workqueue-context helpers (hw-tx, request, firmware, ioctl paths) that are also acquired in code reachable from ndo_start_xmit or TX-completion callbacks that can run under NET_TX/NET_RX softirq — the exact seed shape; branch2=timer-dwork-softirq-lock: find locks acquired inside timer_list, hrtimer, or delayed_work callback bodies (timer softirq context) that are also taken with plain spin_lock from process-context paths (workers, ioctls, open/close, config), yielding softirq-vs-holder deadlock; branch3=tasklet-napi-softirq-lock: find locks shared between process-context code and tasklet_schedule''d functions or NAPI poll / other NET softirq callbacks where the process side uses plain spin_lock instead of spin_lock_bh (excluding xmit and timer callbacks covered by branches 1-2); branch4=hardirq-shared-lock: the interrupt-level analog of the same invariant — locks acquired inside hardirq handlers (request_irq / non-threaded part of request_threaded_irq) that are taken with plain spin_lock (no spin_lock_irqsave/irq) in process or softirq context, allowing the hardirq to preempt and spin on a lock the preempted context can never release.'

Now I need to systematically check each: does the plain spin_lock site pair with a lock used inside a timer callback?

Approach: write a Python script that:
1. For each driver file (drivers/, net/) finds timer_setup / setup_timer / DEFINE_TIMER / INIT_DELAYED_WORK / hrtimer_init sites.
2. Extracts the callback function name.
3. Extracts each callback's body and records spinlock objects acquired within (plain spin_lock(&obj), spin_lock_bh, spin_lock_irqsave, etc. — but for the timer side, plain is fine since timer context is softirq; the bug is on the process side).
4. For each such lock object, searches the whole snapshot for process-context plain spin_lock(&obj) sites.

Callback body extraction: simple brace matching from the function definition.

Also delayed_work: INIT_DELAYED_WORK(&dev->work, fn) — fn runs in process (kworker) context, NOT softirq! Important: delayed_work timers expire in TIMER softirq but only the delayed_work_timer_fn runs there, which calls __queue_work → the work item body runs in a kthread worker. So delayed_work callbacks are process context. The intent says "delayed_work timer-expiry callbacks" — but strictly the work function runs in kworker context. However the intent description counts "delayed_work timer-expiry callbacks" as timer-softirq context. To be safe I'll focus on true timer_list/hrtimer callbacks; delayed_work bodies run in kworker process context so plain spin_lock there vs process-context holders is not a softirq issue. I'll note that.

import re, os, sys, subprocess, json

ROOT = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s09"

def find_files():
    out = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/rg","-l",
        r"timer_setup\(|setup_timer\(|DEFINE_TIMER\(|\.function\s*=|hrtimer_init\(|DEFINE_TIMER",
        "drivers","net","kernel","mm","fs","block","ipc","security","sound","crypto","virt","io_uring","lib",
        "--type","c"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return [f for f in out.stdout.splitlines() if f]

# callback registration patterns
REG = [
    re.compile(r"timer_setup\(\s*&?[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,"),
    re.compile(r"setup_timer\(\s*&?[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,"),
    re.compile(r"DEFINE_TIMER\([^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\)"),
    re.compile(r"\.function\s*=\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,?\s*\n"),
    re.compile(r"hrtimer_init\([^;]*?;"),
]

LOCK = re.compile(r"spin_lock(?:_bh|_irqsave|_irq)?\(\s*&([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.>\-]*)")
PLAIN = re.compile(r"spin_lock\(\s*&([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.>\-]*)")

def func_body(src, name):
    # find definition: name(...) at start of line-ish, followed by {
    pat = re.compile(r"(?:^|\n)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_ \t\*]*\b" + re.escape(name) + r"\s*\([^;{]*?\)\s*\{")
    m = pat.search(src)
    if not m:
        # static inline / __always_inline variants
        pat = re.compile(r"(?:^|\n).*?\b" + re.escape(name) + r"\s*\([^;{]*?\)\s*\{")
        m = pat.search(src)
        if not m:
            return None, None, None
    start = src.find("{", m.start())
    depth = 0
    i = start
    while i < len(src):
        c = src[i]
        if c == "{": depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return start, src[start:i+1], src[:start].count("\n")+1
        i += 1
    return start, src[start:], src[:start].count("\n")+1

results = []
files = find_files()
print(f"files with timer registrations: {len(files)}", file=sys.stderr)
for rel in files:
    try:
        src = open(os.path.join(ROOT, rel), errors="replace").read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    callbacks = set()
    for rx in REG:
        for m in rx.finditer(src):
            for g in m.groups():
                if g and re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$", g):
                    callbacks.add(g)
    if not callbacks: continue
    for cb in callbacks:
        # only consider functions defined in this file
        s, body, lineno = func_body(src, cb)
        if body is None: continue
        locks = LOCK.findall(body)
        plainlocks = PLAIN.findall(body)
        if locks:
            results.append((rel, lineno, cb, sorted(set(locks)), sorted(set(plainlocks))))

for rel, lineno, cb, locks, plain in results:
    print(f"{rel}:{lineno} TIMER_CB {cb} locks={locks} plain_in_timer={plain}")
PYEOF
python3 "$TMPDIR/timerlock.py" > "$TMPDIR/timer_cb_locks.txt" 2> "$TMPDIR/timer_cb_locks.err"; wc -l "$TMPDIR/timer_cb_locks.txt"; head -5 "$TMPDIR/timer_cb_locks.err"
